Code reference¶

Models¶

Normalised editorial records, role relationships and delivery audit state.

class publishing.models.User(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

An account with a unique email and one reader/editorial role.

save synchronises the managed role group and clears relations that no longer fit that role. Subscriptions use normal many-to-many relations; public properties return None when they do not apply. Passwords use AbstractUser’s normal hashing and validation workflow.

class Role(*values)[source]¶

Define the roles used by signup and managed auth groups.

save(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Synchronise managed groups and clear inapplicable subscriptions.

property publisher_subscriptions¶

Expose reader-only subscriptions, or None for editorial accounts.

property journalist_subscriptions¶

Expose reader-only author subscriptions, otherwise None.

property independent_articles¶

Return a journalist’s independently published work, otherwise None.

property independent_newsletters¶

Return independent journalist newsletters, otherwise None.

class publishing.models.Publisher(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

A named publisher with journalist and editor memberships.

The name is unique and description is optional. Membership choices are restricted by role in forms/admin. Readers subscribe through User.followed_publishers rather than copied subscriber records.

exception DoesNotExist¶
exception MultipleObjectsReturned¶
exception NotUpdated¶
class publishing.models.Article(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

A titled article with a journalist author and approval state.

New articles start as drafts. publisher may be NULL for independent work; clean checks the author’s role and publisher membership. Forms call model validation; API serializers perform corresponding checks. Deleting a publisher preserves the article and its author.

clean()[source]¶

Reject non-journalist authors and unrelated publisher assignments.

exception DoesNotExist¶
exception MultipleObjectsReturned¶
exception NotUpdated¶
class publishing.models.Newsletter(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

A collection with an author, description and article links.

Journalists and editors may author newsletters. clean checks the role and optional publisher membership. Forms allow approved article selections. Display/API code also filters drafts because a linked article may return to draft after the newsletter has been saved.

clean()[source]¶

Disallow reader-authored newsletters and unrelated publishers.

exception DoesNotExist¶
exception MultipleObjectsReturned¶
exception NotUpdated¶
class publishing.models.ApprovalDelivery(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Store one approval-delivery record and its recipient snapshot.

A unique article relation prevents competing delivery ledgers. email_sent and http_sent track the steps separately; last_error records a pending delivery message. The service retries incomplete steps without repeating an already-recorded successful mail send.

exception DoesNotExist¶
exception MultipleObjectsReturned¶
exception NotUpdated¶
class publishing.models.ApprovalLog(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Record when the internal API first logged an approved article.

The unique article relation makes repeated HTTP POSTs idempotent. The receiver checks the server secret and approval state before creating this record. received_at is the first receipt timestamp.

Forms¶

Browser forms with explicit field allowlists and role-scoped choices.

class publishing.forms.RegistrationForm(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Register a reader or journalist using Django’s password checks.

The public role field has no editor option; a trusted administrator assigns that role. Email is normalised and checked for duplicates. The shared template supplies labels, help text and errors for the generated Django form widgets.

clean_email()[source]¶

Normalise addresses and reject case-insensitive duplicate accounts.

property media¶

Return all media required to render the widgets on this form.

class publishing.forms.ArticleForm(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Edit an article’s title, content and permitted publisher.

author and approved are excluded to prevent identity/approval changes through submitted fields. Pass an instance with its author already assigned. __init__ filters publishers to that author and gives the content textarea 12 rows for longer drafts.

Bind data using ModelForm arguments. For new articles, pass instance=Article(author=request.user) before is_valid(), so affiliation validation sees the server-assigned identity. A failed form retains field errors for the shared browser template.

property media¶

Return all media required to render the widgets on this form.

class publishing.forms.NewsletterForm(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Edit newsletter details and select its approved articles.

Pass an instance with its author assigned. Publisher choices depend on the author’s journalist/editor memberships. Articles use a checkbox group filtered to approved records; the template wraps it in a labelled fieldset. The author is never a submitted field.

property media¶

Return all media required to render the widgets on this form.

class publishing.forms.SubscriptionForm(*args, **kwargs)[source]¶

Choose the logged-in reader’s publishers and journalists.

Both fields use labelled checkbox groups. Journalist choices exclude inactive accounts and non-journalists. No identity or role field is exposed; the view binds request.user and checks reader access before displaying or saving this form.

property media¶

Return all media required to render the widgets on this form.

Browser views¶

HTML editorial screens with authentication, ownership and safe HTTP methods.

publishing.views.check_owner(user, item)[source]¶

Check whether user may change the article or newsletter item.

Editors may manage any item; a journalist must be its author. Return None on success or raise PermissionDenied (HTTP 403).

Parameters:

  • user (publishing.models.User) – The authenticated caller, not a submitted author ID.

  • item – Persisted Article or Newsletter with an author_id.

Returns:

None when the caller may edit the object.

Raises:

django.core.exceptions.PermissionDenied – If the caller is not authorised to change the item.

publishing.views.home(request)[source]¶

Show the reading/review list on GET or HEAD.

Return publishing/home.html with articles. Visitors and readers see approved work only. Journalists also see their own drafts; editors see all drafts so they can review submissions.

publishing.views.register(request)[source]¶

Display signup or register a reader/journalist account.

GET and invalid POST render publishing/form.html with form and title. A valid POST logs in the new user and redirects to home. Public signup cannot create an editor or assign staff permissions.

publishing.views.article_detail(request, pk)[source]¶

Display the article identified by pk on GET or HEAD.

Return publishing/article.html with article and editable. A reader or visitor gets HTTP 404 for a draft, as does a journalist requesting another author’s draft. Editable controls are only a UI hint; mutation views perform their own permission checks.

publishing.views.article_edit(request, pk=None)[source]¶

Display or save an article as a draft.

pk is None for creation or an existing article ID for editing. Only journalists create articles; editors or the owning journalist may edit. GET and invalid POST render form and title through publishing/form.html. Valid POST saves and redirects to article detail. Editing removes approval so changed content is reviewed.

publishing.views.article_approve(request, pk)[source]¶

Approve article pk and attempt its notifications using POST.

Only an editor may call this view. Missing articles return HTTP 404. The service records approval before contacting mail and the internal API. Set a delivery-status message and redirect to article detail; failed notifications do not turn a saved approval into a new draft.

publishing.views.delete_content(request, kind, pk)[source]¶

Confirm or delete editorial content owned by the caller.

kind comes from the URL configuration and selects Article or Newsletter; pk selects the record. GET renders confirm.html with item. POST deletes and redirects to home or newsletters. A non-owner journalist or reader receives HTTP 403 before deletion.

publishing.views.subscriptions(request)[source]¶

Display or save the logged-in reader’s followed sources.

GET and invalid POST render form and title through publishing/form.html. A valid POST saves the reader’s selections and redirects to subscriptions. Other roles receive HTTP 403. The account is request.user, never a submitted user ID.

publishing.views.newsletters(request)[source]¶

List newsletter collections on GET or HEAD.

Return publishing/newsletters.html with newsletters, newest first. This public list shows collection metadata, not draft article text.

publishing.views.newsletter_detail(request, pk)[source]¶

Show newsletter pk and its currently approved contents.

GET or HEAD renders publishing/newsletter.html with newsletter, articles and editable. Missing IDs return HTTP 404. Filtering at display time also hides a story that was approved when selected but has since returned to draft after an edit.

publishing.views.newsletter_edit(request, pk=None)[source]¶

Display or save a journalist/editor’s newsletter.

pk is None for a new collection or selects an existing newsletter. Readers are denied; editing also checks ownership/editor status. GET and invalid POST render form and title through publishing/form.html. A valid POST redirects to newsletter detail.

Approval services¶

Publication workflow with persisted, independently retryable delivery steps.

publishing.services.approve_article(article_id, editor)[source]¶

Approve article_id as editor and return its delivery record.

Raise PermissionDenied for another role, or Article.DoesNotExist for a missing ID. Commit approval and a recipient snapshot before the delivery attempt so the separate HTTP receiver can read the article. A repeated call reuses the ledger; check its email_sent, http_sent and last_error fields rather than assuming every delivery succeeded.

Parameters:

  • article_id (int) – Primary key of the article being published.

  • editor (publishing.models.User) – Authenticated user whose role must be editor.

Returns:

Delivery ledger, including outstanding notification errors.

Return type:

publishing.models.ApprovalDelivery

Raises:

  • django.core.exceptions.PermissionDenied – If the caller is not an editor.

  • publishing.models.Article.DoesNotExist – If the article ID is missing.

publishing.services.deliver_approval(delivery_id)[source]¶

Retry delivery_id and return the updated delivery record.

Lock the ledger while checking and updating each completion flag. Mail/HTTP failures are recorded in last_error rather than undoing publication; database errors are not swallowed. A successful mail flag is retained when only the HTTP step needs another attempt. This reduces retry duplicates, but SMTP is not exactly-once across a crash between sending and persisting the completion flag.

Parameters:

delivery_id (int) – Primary key of an existing delivery ledger.

Returns:

The ledger with independently persisted email/HTTP flags.

Return type:

publishing.models.ApprovalDelivery

Raises:

publishing.models.ApprovalDelivery.DoesNotExist – If the ledger ID is missing.
